name: S2160 by-design-FP: id-identity entity/auth subclasses
description: java:S2160 (subclass adds fields to a class with equals) is a standing by-design FP for all 11 sites. TWO shapes, both intentional: (1) JPA entities — AbstractAuditableEntity defines equals/hashCode BY ID ONLY, Hibernate.getClass-proxy-safe, class-based CONSTANT hashCode (comment lines 100-123). Subclasses (AbstractSecuredEntity tags, AbstractHierarchicalEntity path, example *Entity/Team/User/TeamMembership/TagDefinition/RoleDefinitionEntity name/etc) MUST inherit it — adding mutable business fields to equals is the actual JPA anti-pattern (breaks null-id->assigned-id set membership + entity-vs-proxy equality). (2) AbacAuthentication extends Spring AbstractAuthenticationToken whose equals already compares principal(=subject.id())+authorities(=ROLE_ from subject.roles())+credentials+details+authenticated; the added transient 'subject' field is fully derivable from principal+authorities, so overriding equals would be redundant and risk breaking Spring's token-comparison contract. NOT a bug/vuln (CODE_SMELL/MINOR). Do not re-fix.

name: S2077 by-design-FP: ltree native SQL interpolates only an allow-listed table identifier
description: java:S2077 (dynamic SQL) at HierarchicalPathMaintainer.java:165 (opa-abac-spring-data, rewriteSubtree UPDATE), CatalogHierarchyService.java:98 (example lockParentRow SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), HierarchyConfig.java:41 (example ltreePathSource SELECT path::text) — ALL by-design FP. In every case the ONLY string-interpolated fragment is the physical TABLE NAME (a SQL identifier, which cannot be a JDBC bind parameter); every user-influenced VALUE (id, oldDepth, path) is a bound setParameter/CAST(? AS uuid|ltree). The table is never attacker-influenced: library site regex-validates via assertSafeIdentifier([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)?) before rewriteSubtree, and its callers pass hardcoded literals ("category"/"product"); both example sites resolve the table through a closed switch allow-list (tableFor / lockParentRow) mapping resource type to catalog/category/product or throwing/empty. Standard unavoidable ltree pattern. NOT re-fixable; the library site already carries the documented assertSafeIdentifier defense.

name: S6353 by-design-FP: explicit [A-Za-z0-9_] on injection-boundary allowlists
description: java:S6353 (MINOR, 'use \w instead of [A-Za-z0-9_]') is a by-design FP at the two injection-boundary allowlists in opa-abac-spring-data/hierarchy: HierarchicalPathMaintainer.assertSafeIdentifier (SQL-identifier injection defense for the native re-parent UPDATE table name) and HierarchyLabels.encodeId (Postgres ltree legal-char check). Keep the explicit character class: (1) via plain String.matches() Java's \w==ASCII [a-zA-Z0-9_] so they are equal TODAY (no functional bug either way -> not gate-critical), BUT (2) the explicit form is defense-in-depth: if the pattern is ever recompiled with UNICODE_CHARACTER_CLASS/(?U), \w silently widens to Unicode letters/digits, broadening a SQLi/ltree-injection boundary; [A-Za-z0-9_] cannot silently widen. (3) The class mirrors an externally-documented constraint (SQL identifier grammar; Postgres ltree accepts only [A-Za-z0-9_], documented in HierarchyLabels javadoc lines 13-16). Do not auto-fix; suppress/accept as FP.

name: S6809 by-design-FP: self-invoked @Transactional callee is REQUIRED with an already-open caller tx
description: java:S6809 (self-invocation of @Transactional bypasses the Spring proxy) fires at 2 sites, both by-design FP: (1) AbstractCrudService.mutate() [opa-abac-spring-data, PUBLISHED] calls getByIdForUpdate(id) directly — the documented safe-by-default write pattern (mx-39d20e); (2) EffectiveRoleService.managementRole() [example app] calls membership(). At BOTH sites the CALLER is itself @Transactional and the CALLEE uses default REQUIRED propagation (no REQUIRES_NEW/Propagation override anywhere in the repo; no @Async/@Cacheable/@Retryable). So the ambient tx is already open and even an honored proxy would just JOIN it (mx-493bd2 confirms getByIdForUpdate JOINS the caller's physical tx) — proxied vs self-invoked are byte-identical: the FOR UPDATE lock (site 1) and the readOnly read (site 2) run inside the caller's tx exactly as intended. S6809 is only a real bug when the callee needs DIFFERENT semantics (REQUIRES_NEW / different readOnly) or the caller has NO tx. Neither holds here. Re-check verdict flips to 'fix' only if a callee ever gets REQUIRES_NEW / distinct propagation or a caller loses @Transactional.

name: S5998 by-design-FP: SAFE_PATH allowlist regex is linear (disjoint '/' delimiter, no ReDoS)
description: java:S5998 (BUG/MAJOR, gate-critical) flags HttpOpaClient.java:47 SAFE_PATH = Pattern.compile("[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)*") as 'repetition can cause stack overflow / catastrophic backtracking'. FALSE POSITIVE. The (…+)* shape only backtracks catastrophically when the inner group can consume the SAME characters as the outer repetition (e.g. (a+)+, ([a-z]+)*). Here the inner group is anchored by a literal '/', which is NOT in the character class [A-Za-z0-9_-]. The '/' positions are unambiguous delimiters, so there is exactly one partition of any input — no exponential re-splitting. Empirically verified linear: fullmatch on non-matching tails up to 120k chars scaled strictly linearly (~2ms at 120k). Also: this regex IS a security control (injection-boundary allowlist preventing OPA-document path traversal '.'/'..' and compile-query splicing; see Javadoc lines 40-46), applied via requireSafePath to a short resolver-derived policy path, not attacker-controlled free text. Do not 'fix'. If Sonar must be silenced, an inline // NOSONAR on the pattern is acceptable; no code change needed. Sibling FP class to S6353 already recorded for the same allowlists.

name: S5841 CONFIRMED-BUG (not FP): vacuous doesNotContain in HierarchyListFilterIT I6
description: S5841 at HierarchyListFilterIT.java:161 is a REAL test-only defect, NOT a by-design FP (contrast S6353/S2160/S2077/S6809/S5998 which ARE by-design). I6 denyOverrides_excludesDeniedRowFromWidenedList asserts .doesNotContain(catDeny) on inheritRows without first proving inheritRows non-empty; SUBJ_INHERIT's tag residual is denyAll() so it depends ENTIRELY on subtreeSpec widening — and AbacQueryService.findAuthorized has fail-closed return List.of() paths (DENY_ALL branch etc). A widening regression -> empty list -> line 161 passes vacuously, masking exactly the MANDATORY deny-override guarantee. Non-empty content (catEmea,catApac) is only proven in sibling widening_twoSubjects_differentSets:151, which does NOT protect the independent I6 test. Fix: insert assertThat(inheritRows).contains(catEmea,catApac) before line 161; symmetrically harden line 163 with region subject contains(catEmea). Test-only, additive, superset of what :151 proves exactly -> cannot false-fail on green code. Sonar flagged only 161; 163 is latent-vacuous too.

CORRECTION of the prior FP record mx-2fcf40. java:S5998 on HttpOpaClient.java:47 SAFE_PATH = Pattern.compile("[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)*") is a GENUINE defect. The prior triage only refuted CATASTROPHIC BACKTRACKING (ReDoS time-blowup) and confirmed linear time to 120k chars — but S5998's actual finding message is 'Refactor this repetition that can lead to a stack overflow for large inputs.' The (…/…)* construct compiles to a RECURSIVE Loop/GroupHead/GroupTail match chain in java.util.regex; each '/'-delimited segment adds stack frames. EMPIRICALLY on JDK 25 default stack: SAFE_PATH.matcher(path).matches() throws java.lang.StackOverflowError at ~5000 segments (input length ~10001 chars) for BOTH matching (a/a/a/…/a) and non-matching (a/a/…/! ) inputs. WORSE: StackOverflowError extends Error, NOT Exception, and all three call sites (allow L108, compile L170, allowAll) catch only 'Exception e' — so the SOE ESCAPES the fail-closed catch (proven: a mirror of requireSafePath+allow's try/catch let the SOE propagate uncaught out of the catch(Exception) deny path). Impact: a ~10k-char resolver-derived policy PATH (type segment) turns a clean 403 deny into an uncaught Error / 500, defeating the fail-closed guarantee for that input. Reachability: type comes from context.resource().type(); in the shipped example it's a compile-time literal ('catalog'/'product'), so NOT exploitable as-shipped — but HttpOpaClient/PolicyPathResolver/@OpaPreAuthorize(resourceType=<SpEL>) are PUBLIC library extension points and SAFE_PATH is explicitly the untrusted-input allowlist ('whatever the PolicyPathResolver implementation returned'), so a consumer binding a request-derived type is unguarded.
resolution: FIX, do not silence. Replace the recursive-repetition regex with a linear form that validates the same grammar without per-segment recursion, e.g. anchored ^[A-Za-z0-9_/-]+$ plus explicit rejection of leading/trailing '/', empty segments, and '.'/'..' — or a non-regex char-scan. Alternatively add a hard length cap on the resolved path BEFORE the regex (paths are short by design) and/or catch Throwable (not just Exception) at the fail-closed boundary so an SOE still denies. The prior 'inline // NOSONAR, no code change' guidance is WRONG for this rule. Supersedes mx-2fcf40 (that record's 'no ReDoS' analysis is correct but ADDRESSES THE WRONG FAILURE MODE).

During the 2026-07-15 Sonar baseline triage, the per-rule adjudicator marked S5998 on HttpOpaClient.SAFE_PATH (regex [A-Za-z0-9_-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)*) a by-design FP by disproving CATASTROPHIC BACKTRACKING (linear to 120k chars — correct, the '/' delimiter is disjoint from the char class). But S5998's actual finding is STACK OVERFLOW: java.util.regex compiles (…/…)* to a recursive Loop/GroupHead/GroupTail chain, and ~5000 segments (~10k chars) throws StackOverflowError on JDK 25. Because SOE extends Error (not Exception), it ESCAPES the catch(Exception) fail-closed handler in allow/compile/allowAll → a clean 403 deny becomes an uncaught 500, defeating fail-closed. Reachable via the public PolicyPathResolver / @OpaPreAuthorize(resourceType=SpEL) extension points. The adversarial-verify skeptic (prompted to REFUTE, default-to-real on gate-critical) reproduced the SOE and flipped FP to FIX. Single-pass adjudication had shipped the wrong verdict; adversarial verification with a real repro caught it.
resolution: Replaced the recursive-repetition regex with a linear, non-recursive isSafePath() char-scan + a 512-char MAX_PATH_LENGTH cap in HttpOpaClient; added regression test U9d (a ~40k-char path fails closed with no StackOverflowError). When judging a Sonar finding, read the rule's OWN hazard (S5998 = stack overflow, not ReDoS) before disproving a different one; and treat a fail-closed catch(Exception) as a latent escape for any Error.

title: S6474 Gradle dependency verification: accepted-risk (no full verification-metadata.xml) for this solo public repo
rationale: Decided 2026-07-15. Inbound resolution is mavenCentral()+Gradle-plugin-portal over TLS with signed artifacts, and the Gradle distribution is now SHA-pinned (distributionSha256Sum). Full gradle/verification-metadata.xml was rejected: the graph has ~201 runtime deps incl. net.java.dev.jna (per-OS native artifacts) + Testcontainers, and CI is ubuntu-latest while dev is macOS-aarch64 — so it needs multi-classifier entries and breaks one env whenever a classifier is missing, plus regeneration on every dep/plugin bump. For a single-maintainer public portfolio repo (no privileged deploy target, no secret-exfil build surface) the residual is bounded; full per-artifact verification is enterprise-CI hygiene whose marginal gain doesn't cover the maintenance + cross-platform-CI-break cost. Recorded, not silently suppressed: the S6474 instance is won't-fix in the local Sonar DB. RE-EVALUATE if the repo gains a privileged CI deploy step or a second maintainer.

description: Discovered when the baseline was CLEAN (0 open findings) but the gate still read ERROR. Only new_coverage was failing; all four issue-conditions were OK. The gate 'OPA-ABAC Local — no new issues' had 7 conditions, not the 3 the bootstrap intended — the extras were inherited on create. Cleaned the live gate (delete_condition) + patched bootstrap.sh + verified a fresh gate now has exactly 3 conditions and reads OK.
resolution: bootstrap.sh now strips EVERY inherited condition from the freshly-created gate before adding new_bugs/new_vulnerabilities/new_code_smells (GT 0). Root cause: api/qualitygates/create on 26.x copies the built-in 'Sonar way' conditions (new_coverage>=80, duplication, hotspots) into the new gate; the scan runs testClasses with no jacoco → 0% coverage imported → new_coverage condition can never pass, so the gate reads ERROR even at 0 findings. The findings count (and the changed-files scan) is the real signal; the aggregate gate badge only recomputes on the next analysis, so after mutating issues/conditions you must re-scan to see the true status.

name: S1075 by-design-FP: a downstream API-version path constant in a proxy client
description: java:S1075 ('get this URI from a customizable parameter') fires on CatalogTools.CATALOGS_PATH = '/api/v1/catalogs' in example-mcp-server. BY-DESIGN FP for this class: the DEPLOYMENT variable is the host, and it already IS configurable (example.mcp.catalog.base-url, McpServerProperties.Catalog#baseUrl); the path is the downstream service's API-VERSION CONTRACT, which the proxy is written against and which changes only when the client code changes. Promoting it to a property would let a deployment repoint the tools at an arbitrary path - a WIDER surface, not a safer one - and would decouple the constant from the DTO shapes the same class parses. Note the finding only appeared AFTER fixing S1192 (duplicated literal x3) by extracting the constant: the two rules pull in opposite directions on the same code, and the extraction is still the right call because the resulting catalogPath(id) helper makes it structurally impossible for an id to reach a path without going through segment() percent-encoding. Expect this class to recur in any future client module that proxies a versioned REST API.

name: S3011 by-design-FP: setAccessible in a deliberately-reflective, deliberately-disposable SDK adapter
description: S3011 ('This accessibility update should be removed') on example-mcp-server RosterFilterInstaller is a by-design FP, not a finding to re-fix. Reflection IS the class's whole purpose and is the documented mechanism (00-DESIGN 3.2, ADR 0028): MCP Java SDK 2.0.0 exposes NO supported seam for varying tools/list per caller — the handler is a private lambda in a package-private requestHandlers map — so two reflective field reads are the only way in until java-sdk #578 (SDK 2.1) ships a pluggable ToolsRepository, at which point the whole class is deleted. The reflection is isolated to that one class by design precisely so the FP has a single, disposable home. Do NOT silence it globally and do NOT 'fix' it by moving the reflection elsewhere. Recorded 2026-07-31 (T5). Baseline context: changed-files scan went 37 -> 41 findings in T5; the delta is this one new class plus three test-style instances of already-standing classes (S5778, S5853, S2925). The two findings in T5 that WERE real (S2583 dead null-branch, S2259 reachable NPE in the reflective walk) were fixed, not filed.

title: S1168 (return empty instead of null) on OpaPreAuthorizeAuthorizationManager.resolveRootAttributes is a BY-DESIGN false positive
rationale: ADR 0032's root-attribute enrichment has THREE wire states and the whole tier contract rests on telling two of them apart: ABSENT root_attributes = the tier is UNPROVEN (enrichment failed) -> a supervised read is CLOSED; an EMPTY MAP {} = the root was fetched and carries no tags -> non-production -> OPEN; populated = as tagged. resolveRootAttributes returns null on every failure precisely so the field is OMITTED from the OPA input. Taking Sonar's advice and returning Collections.emptyMap() would serialize as "root_attributes":{} and turn every enrichment outage into 'the root is untagged', OPENING the production tier for supervised reads - the exact fail-open the two-clause Rego shape (mx-df8f2b) exists to prevent, arriving through the Java side instead. Marked false-positive in the local Sonar (2 issues, lines ~423/432) with the same rationale as an issue comment during STEP-UP-ELEVATION T4. NOTE the surfacing mechanism: these lines are PRE-EXISTING (slice B) and only appear in a changed-files scan because slice C edited elsewhere in the same file - a changed-FILE gate resurfaces old by-design findings, so expect to re-triage them whenever a hot file is touched. FP-marking needs basic auth as admin with the local password from .sonar-local/bootstrap.sh (default OpaAbacLocal!2026x), NOT the scanner token: the token returns 401 on /api/issues/*.
